headline: Pats look like world beaters and B's win a shootout thriller
morning_brew: What a wild Saturday in the Hub, starting with the Pats putting on a clinic against the Steelers. Drake Maye looked composed under pressure and TreVeyon Henderson was a force on the ground, making that twenty-point performance feel like a real statement for the squad. It is early, but this team is starting to show the kind of grit we haven't seen in a while, and watching them control the trenches all afternoon was a breath of fresh air that nearly made me forget the price of a beer at Gillette.

Over on the ice, the Bruins pulled off a gritty win in a shootout against the Capitals. It was one of those nail-biters that makes you sweat through your jersey, but Michael DiPietro stood tall in net and young James Hagens showed exactly why he belongs in the mix. Seeing Charlie McAvoy find the back of the net late in the third was pure gold, and clinching it in the skills competition was the kind of victory that had me jumping off my couch and scaring the neighbor's cat.

The Red Sox had a tougher go of it down in Tampa, dropping a decision where the bats just couldn't solve the Rays' arms. Patrick Sandoval battled through the start but the damage early on was too much to overcome, despite Caleb Durbin finding a couple of knocks to keep things moving. We are in the thick of the stretch run and every loss stings, but with some big games against Cleveland coming to the Fens this week, we have to flip the page and get back to work immediately.

news_digest.dans_take: Chad Tracy has this team believing, and honestly, that is half the battle.
